summary: This note is a short biographical sketch of Lee M. Russell. It states he was born in Lafayette County, Mississippi, and attended the University of Mississippi, where he led a movement to abolish Greek fraternities. After graduating in 1901, he attended the University of Mississippi School of Law, was admitted to the bar, and practiced law in Oxford, Mississippi.
one_line: Biographical note on Lee M. Russell, a Mississippi man who led an anti-fraternity movement at the University of Mississippi and later practiced law in Oxford.
key_facts: Lee M. Russell was born in Lafayette County, Mississippi.
Lee M. Russell later attended the University of Mississippi.
While a student at the University of Mississippi, Lee M. Russell was the leader in a movement to abolish Greek fraternities.
Lee M. Russell graduated from the University of Mississippi in 1901.
After graduating in 1901, Lee M. Russell enrolled in the University of Mississippi School of Law.
Lee M. Russell was admitted to the bar after completing the University of Mississippi School of Law course.
Lee M. Russell practiced law in Oxford, Mississippi.
